summary: All 89 Maths leaves have notes, flashcards, a quiz and exam items, and M7.3 is not bare (7 pages, 1,771 words, 15 worked examples, 21 cards); nothing in the Maths content, engines or renderer has changed since the first audit, so all 13 earlier findings hold (the Write-it-out chip now collides with the source line rather than the title). The behaviour inventory adds the engines' judgements: the quiz's authored answer position lets 'A every time' score 69% on M7.3, the 'Retry the N missed' pass overwrites the topic's quiz score with 100% and logs a phantom 4/4 session, and the RAG starts at 100 and subtracts, so one mediocre quiz shows 'Data says Green'. Derived exam items make the Answer line a tickable mark and ignore M1/A1 codes (P1), and 24 worked examples' codes do not add up to their marks. Presentation gaps found by sweeping all 433 note pages: long \displaystyle step lines push the topic page sideways on iPhone, plot labs draw axis numbers at 5.7px on iPhone, four titles show raw carets, and a third of quiz explanations are bare labels. Root causes: generated spec text and titles never cleaned (gen_data.py), bank files added without duplicate/quality checks, worked examples reused as exam items without a mark-code model, and stats/RAG code that assumes one whole-quiz attempt.
coverage:
Build kos-redraw-1 (HEAD f84962c); no commit to any Maths content, spine, engine, renderer, figures, rag, edits or CSS file since the first audit (56b1a8c), so content numbers were re-measured with the node scripts in audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/ and behaviour re-run in the browser (slot 7, empty account, then seeded). findings.title: Specification tab shows garbled PDF-extraction text on most Maths leaves (M7.3 included)
findings.detail: The Spec tab is drawn from js/data/maths.js content/info lines, which are raw, broken PDF extraction. Examples: M7.3 guidance reads "v = u + at r = ut +1at2 / e.g. , with vectors / 2 given in i - j or column vector form". 5.6 reads "Understand and use double a n g le f / rm u l a e ; u s e / f s in ( A ± B ), fo r m u l a e fo r / ± ± cos (A B)". 2.1 reads "× = , ÷ = - , = m n n am / The equivalence ofa and should be known." 2.10 starts mid-sentence: "into partial fractions". 25 leaves still contain the extraction artefact "need to learn:" or "students need to learn:". A heuristic found fragment lines in 36 of the 89 leaves: 1.1 2.1 2.2 2.3 2.4 2.5 2.7 2.9 3.3 4.1 4.2 4.3 5.1 5.2 5.3 5.5 5.6 5.7 6.2 6.3 6.4 7.1 7.2 7.4 8.2 8.3 8.5 8.6 9.4 10.4 S2.3 S4.1 S5.3 M7.4 M8.3 M8.6, and reading the dump shows more. Exponents, fractions, sums and integrals are lost throughout. This is very likely part of why M7.3 looks bare.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-spec-mac.png; shots/content-maths/p5-6-spec-mac.png; cm/spine.txt (every leaf's spec text); tools/gen_data.py:240-255 (maths_group copies clean(x) of the extracted lines) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): Re-shot on kos-redraw-1: shots/content-maths/top-m73-spec-mac.png (Guidance: 'r = ut +1at2', 'e.g. , with vectors', '2 given in i - j'); js/data/maths.js still has 25 'need to learn:'; no commit to tools/gen_data.py or js/data/maths.js since 56b1a8c.
findings.fix: Hand-author the 89 Maths spec entries from the Edexcel 9MA0 PDF as typeset blocks (LaTeX in $…$). Either fix the extractor or add a checked-in override table that gen_data.py applies (as SHORT does), and regenerate. Drop the "need to learn:" headers. Add a smoke test that refuses fragment lines (≤4 characters, runs of single letters, "need to learn").
findings.rootCause: The spec spine is generated from a PDF text extraction (/home/claude/extract) that splits equations and kerned headings, and no override or cleanup pass exists for Maths.

findings.title: Quiz answers are almost always A or B, and options are never shuffled
findings.detail: Of 1,058 Maths quiz items, the correct option is A in 531 and B in 481. Only 44 are C and 2 are D. Base files: 380 A, 100 B, 17 C, 1 D. Bank files: 151 A, 381 B, 27 C, 1 D. KOS.quiz.mountMCQ renders opts in authored order, and its Shuffle button only reorders the questions. A learner soon learns to pick A on a base item or B on a bank item, so the quiz score stops measuring understanding. Separately, the correct option is uniquely the longest in 317 items (30%).
findings.evidence: cm/metrics.json ansDist per leaf; js/engines/quiz.js:66 (Shuffle shuffles order only), :88-96 (item.opts rendered in order, answer compared to item.ans at :113); e.g. js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js:305-306 (every item ans: 0); shots/content-maths/m73-quiz-ipad.png (Q1 answer A) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): Re-measured: base answers A 380/498, bank answers B 381/560 (D appears 1+1 times); js/engines/quiz.js:66 Shuffle reorders questions only, :88-96 options in authored order. New repro: answering A to every question of M7.3 scores 9/13 = 69% (cm/qz-retry.js), which the RAG then reads as Green.
findings.fix: In mountMCQ, shuffle a per-question option permutation at mount and on Retry, seeded per attempt, and map clicks back to the original index so the stats and the why text stay valid. Optionally also rebalance the authored ans positions so a fixed order is fair too.
findings.rootCause: Authors put the right answer first (bank authors second), and the engine trusts the authored order.

findings.title: Exam questions self-mark ignores the M1/A1 codes on Maths worked-derived items, and the Answer line counts as a mark
findings.detail: 592 of the 1,244 Maths exam parts (48%) are derived from exam-style worked examples by KOS.content.examFromWorked. Each mark-scheme point is one STEP, ending in its codes, for example '[M1 A1]', and the worked answer is added as an extra point, '**Answer:** …'. The self-mark tally in js/engines/quiz.js knows nothing about those codes. When the number of points equals the marks (106 parts), each tick counts as 1 mark. When there are more points (112 parts), it caps at the total. When there are fewer (374 parts), it scales the marks in proportion. Repro on maths 1.1 Q1 (3 marks; points '[M1 A1]', '[A1]', 'Answer'): ticking only the Answer line awards 1/3, and ticking only the [M1 A1] step also awards 1/3, when it is worth 2. Each row prints '1' beside it. The needsM rule (an A needs its M) never applies, because the lines start with the working, not with 'A1'. So the logged exam session (KOS.sessions.log type exam, marks/max) records partial marks that do not match the mark scheme it shows. The 652 bank parts are written one point per mark and are correct.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/selfmark-answerline-mac.png (Answer ticked → Awarded 1/3; step 1 shows [M1 A1] but '1'); eval on #/ref/maths/1.1 Exam questions: onlyAnswerTicked '1', onlyStep1Ticked '1'; counts via eval over KOS_CONTENT: derived parts 592 (perMark 106, more 112, fewer 374), bank 652 all perMark; js/core/content.js:547-555 (ms = one line per step + '[mk]', Answer pushed as a point); js/engines/quiz.js:264-268 (needsM tests /^\s*A\d/), :286-296 (perMark / proportional fromTicks)
findings.rootCause: examFromWorked emits one scheme point per step (several marks) plus the answer, but the tally assumes one point = one mark or scales proportionally
findings.fix: In examFromWorked, expand each step into one point per mark code (e.g. '[M1] …', '[A1] …' with the step text on the first), so the scheme is one point per mark like the banks; do not push the Answer as a point (show it as a separate 'Answer' line under the scheme). Alternatively give points a weight parsed from their [codes] and make fromTicks sum weights and needsM read the code tokens. Add a smoke check: Σ point weights = marks for every exam part.

findings.title: "Write it out" chip overlaps worked-example titles on every device and is only 23px tall
findings.detail: On worked cards with more than one step, the "Write it out" pill is position:absolute at the top-right, and the .k-n-worked-head row reserves no room for it. On M7.3's notes it lies over the title or src text on 4 of 15 cards on the Mac (1470), 2 of 15 on iPad portrait, 3 of 15 on iPad landscape and 9 of 15 on iPhone (402). Example on the Mac: "Write it out" is printed over "AS Specimen · P2 Q1(a)(b) · 5 marks". On iPhone it covers "Find the initial velocity". The pill measures 81×23 px with min-block-size:0, below the 44px touch minimum (invariant 69). The same overlap affects every subject's worked cards, because content.js is shared.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/writeout-overlap-mac.png; shots/content-maths/m73-notes-p6-iphone.png; measured: btn rect [233,618,81,23] while .k-n-worked-head starts at y=626, width 334 (iphone); css/views/ink.css:300; js/core/content.js:373; css/views/study.css:346 | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): shots/content-maths/top-writeout-8-3-mac.png ('Write it out' over 'P1 Q5 · 5 marks'); cm/wo2.js output; css/views/ink.css:300 (position:absolute; inset-inline-end calc(var(--sp-8)*9); min-block-size:0).
findings.fix: Put the chip in the head's flex flow (margin-inline-start:auto, before Copy) instead of absolute positioning, or give the head padding-inline-end equal to the chip's and Copy's widths. Raise the hit area to 44px for coarse pointers.
findings.rootCause: An absolutely positioned control added onto a flex header that wraps freely.
findings.recheck: changed: the chip now collides with the source/marks line (k-n-worked-src) rather than the title; 41 of 75 Write-it-out chips in 2.3, 4.1, M7.3, S4.2, 8.3 overlap it on the Mac (cm/wo2.js); still 81x23px on every device

findings.title: A curriculum fork silently hides later curriculum upgrades (plausible cause of "M7.3 is basically bare")
findings.detail: KOS.content.get and srs read state.edits first (invariant 86). A fork copies the shipped material at the moment of the first edit and is never compared with the curriculum again. M7.3 was an outline entry until commit 4d791ca ("load M6–M7 at depth, drop their outline entries"), and a9f64b5 rewrote M7.2 and M7.3. A Notes fork made before then (or one carried over from S7.3 by the ref rename, router.js:117 renamedRef) keeps showing the old, thin outline notes. Nothing tells the user that a newer, much deeper version exists. The only sign is the Edit button's data-state forked (hub.js:2828). The shipped M7.3 renders in full (8 pages), so a bare M7.3 on the user's device most likely comes from such a fork.
findings.evidence: js/core/edits.js:1-60 (no base hash or staleness check: grep for stale/baseHash finds nothing); git log -- js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js (a9f64b5, 4d791ca); shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (shipped content present) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): js/core/edits.js:199-207 set() stores only the kind and updatedAt — no shipped hash or version; fixture: KOS.edits.set('maths','M7.3','notes', first 3 blocks) then reopen: no notice on the Notes tab or inspector (eval, then reset); shots/content-maths/top-m73-forked-mac.png taken after the reset shows the shipped 8 pages.
findings.fix: Record a hash of the shipped kind on each fork (fork.base). When the shipped hash differs, show a banner on the tab: "The curriculum for this topic was updated after you edited it: View new · Keep mine · Merge (append your rows)". Check the user's real state for state.edits.topics['maths:M7.3'] (or 'maths:S7.3').
findings.rootCause: The fork model has no notion of the base version it was taken from.

findings.title: Bank files duplicate base flashcards and quiz items in the same leaf (17 exact repeats, about 45 same-answer groups)
findings.detail: bank-maths-*.js were added without a duplicate check against the base items. Exact repeats in the same quiz include: 2.1 "$8^{2/3}$ =" (qz0 and qz8); 4.1 "$\binom92$" (qz0 and qz18), "Coefficient of $x$ in $(2+x)^5$" (qz8 and qz22), "Coefficient of $x^2$ in $(1+x)(1+4x+6x^2)$" (qz10 and qz24), "$(1+3x)^{-1}$ valid for" (qz4 and qz20); 5.2 "$\sin3\theta\approx$" and "$1-\cos2\theta\approx$" both twice; 5.3 "$\tan\frac{3\pi}4$" twice; 5.6 "$\cos(A-B)$" twice; 6.3 "$\log_{10}0.001$" twice; 2.6 "$(x-2)$ is a factor means" twice; 2.8 "inverse only if one-to-one" twice; 7.2 "$d/dx\sqrt x$" twice. Flashcard and quiz pairs on the same fact: M7.3 "Which equation has no t?" (fc1 and qz10, and qz1 again); M7.5 time of flight and greatest height; 8.5 "∫ln x"; 7.5 "d/dx(3y²)"; 3.3 parametric dy/dx; 10.3 midpoint; 8.1 states the FTC twice (fc0 and fc5b) and uses the same f′ setup twice (fc4 and fc6b); 6.1 has "$e^{2x}=5$" as fc10b and qz3, "features of $a^x$" as fc0 and fc7b, and the asymptotes of $e^x+3$ and $e^x+2$ as qz0 and qz6b; 10.4 has "|AC| = 4 with one unknown" three times. Cross-leaf: S4.2 and S4.3 repeat continuity-correction cards, and S4.1 and S5.2 repeat "$P(X\ge k)$ in cumulative form". Full list: cm/dups2.json (66 within-leaf pairs, 14 cross-leaf pairs, 45 same-answer groups).
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/cm/dups2.json; e.g. js/data/content/maths-pure-p8.js:505 vs bank-maths-pure-c.js:457 ("Before integrating x²/(x−1) you should") | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): Re-run cm/dups2.js: 66 near-duplicate pairs inside a leaf, 17 exact repeats (e.g. 2.1 '$8^{2/3}$ =' qz0 and qz8b; 4.1 four exact repeats; M7.3 fc1 = qz10b), 27 same-answer pairs, 14 near-duplicates across leaves; no content commit since 56b1a8c.
findings.fix: Delete or replace the bank items flagged in dups2.json with new item shapes. Add a smoke test that canonicalises q and the answer (\dfrac→\frac, strip spaces) and fails on an exact or same-answer duplicate inside one leaf. Removing flashcards must follow invariant 87 (carry the original index as a third element).
findings.rootCause: KOS.content.extend concatenates bank arrays blindly, and no test checks for duplicates.

The median leaf is about 1,040 words, and 4.1 has 8,667 words and 31 worked examples. 7.2 and 8.2 carry most of Paper 1 and 2 calculus but have the depth of a summary. Leaves with 5 or fewer exam items: 2.11 3.4 4.6 5.3 5.4 6.1 6.2 8.1 8.4 8.6 8.8 9.5 S4.3 M8.1 M8.3 M8.5.
findings.evidence: cm/metrics.json; table printed by cm/metrics.js; shots/content-maths/p8-4-notes-mac.png (8.4 is one short page) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): Re-run cm/metrics.js: 8.4 185 words (one page), 8.1 235, 6.1 302, 6.2 331, 4.3 413, 7.2 439 vs 4.1 8,667; 6.2, 8.1 and 8.4 have no page markers at all.
findings.fix: Run the per-section depth pipeline used for 4.1, 2.x and M7 on P6 (6.1–6.5), P7.2, P8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.6, 8.8, 4.3, 4.6, 5.4, 10.4, 9.5, S4.3 and M8.3. Target at least 3 pages, at least 5 exam-tagged worked examples with Edexcel marks, a figure where a picture helps, and an exam toolkit page.
findings.rootCause: The depth rewrite stopped short on P6 to P8 and several small leaves. The files for P1, P9, P10 and M7 to M9 are dated 8 October and P2 to P8 27 October, and the light leaves were never brought up to the contract.

findings.title: Statistics and Mechanics leaf titles are cut-off 80-character spec sentences, unlike the short Pure titles
findings.detail: Pure leaves have names like "Straight lines" and "Trapezium rule". Every S and M leaf is titled with the first 80 characters of its spec sentence plus "…", e.g. M7.3 "Understand, use and derive the formulae for constant acceleration for motion in …" and S4.1 "simple, discrete probability distributions" (lowercase fragment). The page title is then cut again to three lines with an ellipsis, the spine rows read "Understand and use the lang…" five times in a row under M7, and the search results and breadcrumbs show the same. gen_data.py already defines SHORT_S ("suvat (constant acceleration)", "Projectiles", …), but it is never applied to the checked-in maths.js. Its keys are bare ("7.3") while the payload's refs are "S1.1" and "M7.3", and the generator cannot run locally (it reads /home/claude/extract).
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (title and spine); shots/content-maths/m73-notes-iphone.png; tools/gen_data.py:249 (80-char truncation), :287-301 (SHORT_S and its lookup by c["ref"]); js/data/maths.js:989 ("S1.1"), :1287 ("M7.3") | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): 21 of 89 leaf titles still end in '…' (every S and M leaf longer than 80 characters); spine in shots/content-maths/top-m73-spec-mac.png ('simple, discrete probability di…' starts lower-case); tools/gen_data.py:249 and the SHORT_S lookup by c['ref'] ('S1.1') against keys like '1.1'.
findings.fix: Key SHORT_S by the final refs (S1.1…S5.3, M6.1…M9.1) and add a payload-only pass, like --mech-refs, that applies titles to the checked-in maths.js. Then regenerate.
findings.rootCause: The short-title table is keyed by refs that never match the stats and mech children, and the generator's source is not available to re-run.

findings.title: Wrong flashcard answer: 9.3 Newton–Raphson from x0 = 0 gives x1 = −2.5, not 2.5
findings.detail: 9.3 FC5 (bank) asks "Why does $x_0 = 0$ fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" and answers "it does not fail here; $x_1 = 2.5$". In fact f(0) = −5 and f′(0) = −2, so x1 = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5, which the card's own formula (2x³+5)/(3x²−2) also gives. The question also states something false: it says the method fails and the answer says it does not.
findings.evidence: js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-c.js:646 | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-c.js:646 unchanged: answer says '$x_1 = 2.5$'; x1 = 0 − f(0)/f'(0) = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5.
findings.fix: Rewrite the card, e.g. "Where would NR fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" → "Where $f'(x_0)=0$: $x_0=\pm\sqrt{2/3}$". Or keep the x0 = 0 example with "$x_1=-2.5$ (far from the root 2.09)". Keep its schedule key (invariant 87).
findings.rootCause: An arithmetic sign slip in the bank author's answer, with no automated check on numeric answers.

findings.title: 24 exam-style worked examples carry mark codes that do not add up to their stated marks
findings.detail: An exam-style worked example states its total in src (e.g. '· 11 marks'), and each step carries its Edexcel codes (mk). In 24 of the 604 Maths exam-tagged examples, the codes add up to a different total. Examples: 5.9 'Tide model' is stated as 11 marks, but its codes (B1 M1 A1 · B1 · B1 · M1 A1 A1) add up to 8. 3.4 'The dam' is stated as 11, with codes adding up to 8. 8.3 'Equal areas either side of the axis' is stated as 10, with codes adding up to 8. 5.1 'Badge' is stated as 4, with codes adding up to 5. 2.3 'Complete the square, sketch…' is stated as 10, with codes adding up to 11. A learner reading the model answer cannot tell where the missing marks come from, or why there are extra ones, and the derived exam item (marks = src) inherits the inconsistency. Full list: 2.3×2, 2.6, 2.7×2, 2.8, 3.2, 3.4×2, 4.1×2, 5.1, 5.7, 5.9×2, 6.6×2, 7.6, 8.3×2, 8.5, 8.7, S2.4, S4.2.
findings.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/mk2.js output (24 rows: leaf | title | stated | sum of step codes); e.g. node cm/mk.js 'Tide model' → mks ["B1 M1 A1","B1","B1","M1 A1 A1"] vs src 'A-level Specimen · P1 Q13 · 11 marks'
findings.rootCause: Hand-authored mk codes, with no check that their sum equals the src mark count (smoke65/66 hold CS to a depth contract; Maths has no equivalent mark-sum lint)
findings.fix: Correct each of the 24 from the published mark scheme: add the missing codes or fix the total. Add a lint (in the Maths smoke) that the sum of the codes equals the src marks for every exam-tagged worked example.

findings.title: Newton–Raphson generator prints a 'Root estimate' that is not a root in about a third of its random examples
findings.detail: The worked-example generator 'newraph', wired to 9.3, always does exactly three iterations from a random x0 and then prints 'Root estimate: x ≈ …', whatever f is at that point. In 138 of 400 random examples, |f(x3)| > 0.01. Two cases: x^3 − 2x − 5 from x0 = 1 gives 'x ≈ 3.34870 (f ≈ 25.85)' (the true root is 2.0946), and x^3 + x − 1 from x0 = 3 gives 'x ≈ 0.88069 (f ≈ 0.564)' (the true root is 0.6823). A learner using the generator to check their own working is taught that a non-converged value is the answer.
findings.evidence: eval on slot 7: 400 runs of KOS.worked.byIds(['newraph'])[0] → bad 138; examples quoted above; js/labs/worked.js:704 (Root estimate step printed unconditionally after three iterations)
findings.fix: Iterate until |x_{n+1} − x_n| < 1e-6 (cap about 20) and show the first three steps plus 'converges to …'. Or pick x0 near a root (from a sign change). If it does not converge, say so ('not converged yet: f(x3) = …').

findings.title: 'Retry the N missed' overwrites the topic's quiz score with the retry's: 9/13 then 4/4 records lastPct 100 and the head reads 'best 9/4'
findings.detail: After a quiz, 'Retry the N missed' (js/engines/quiz.js:178-181) mounts the SAME engine on the missed subset with the topic's own stats record. finish() (quiz.js:156-160) then sets lastPct = correct / subset size, logs a second 'quiz' session with total = the subset, and the head line compares the stored best (a count out of the full quiz) with the subset length. Repro on #/ref/maths/M7.3 (empty account): answer every question with A → 9/13, record {attempts 1, best 9, lastPct 69}; press 'Retry the 4 missed', answer them right → record {attempts 2, best 9, lastPct 100}, sessions [{9/13 69%}, {4/4 100%}], head 'score 4 · best 9/4'. RAG reads lastPct (js/modules/rag.js:63-71), so a learner who got 69% now shows no quiz weakness at all, and the ledger/Reports count a 100% quiz that never happened.
findings.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/qz-retry.js (eval on slot 7, output quoted); shots/content-maths/top-quizbest-inspector-mac.png ('best 9/13', inspector 'Quiz attempts 2', 'Data says Green'); js/engines/quiz.js:156-165, :178-181; js/modules/rag.js:63-71
findings.fix: Pass a 'practice' flag for the missed retry: do not touch st.lastPct/best (or record it under a separate missedRetry field), log it as a practice session (or not at all), and print the head as 'retrying 4 missed' instead of best/total.
findings.rootCause: The missed-retry reuses mountMCQ's normal finish path, which assumes items is the topic's whole quiz.

findings.title: One mediocre quiz makes a Maths topic 'Data says Green': the RAG starts at 100 and a 69% quiz only takes 8 points off
findings.detail: rag.auto (js/modules/rag.js:30-110) starts every topic at score 100 and SUBTRACTS for weak signals; band() (rag.js:17) is Green from 70. With only a quiz as evidence, the most a quiz can remove is 25 (lastPct 0 %), so ANY single quiz attempt — even 0 % — leaves the topic Amber or Green, and a 69 % quiz removes 8 → Green. Thin evidence (one quiz, no cards rated, no exam questions, 0/4 checks, status Not started) is judged as mastery. Repro: empty account, M7.3, quiz answered all-A (9/13 = 69 %): inspector shows 'Data says Green' beside 'Not started' and '0/4 checks'. The answer-position bias (all-A scores 69 %) makes this reachable without reading a single question.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/top-quizbest-inspector-mac.png; js/modules/rag.js:17 (band), :63-71 (quiz penalty capped at 25), :103 (no minimum evidence); eval qz-retry.js before the retry: lastPct 69 → band g
findings.fix: Make the auto band evidence-weighted: start from 'no claim' and require a minimum amount of evidence (e.g. ≥ N cards rated or a quiz ≥ 80 % plus another signal) before Green; map a lone quiz to a score proportional to its percentage rather than a capped deduction.
findings.rootCause: Subtractive scoring from 100 with capped penalties and no evidence threshold.

findings.title: Long worked-step lines push the topic page sideways on iPhone: 14 lines in 9 Maths leaves run up to 114px past the screen
findings.devices: iPhone (402px); not on iPad 820 or Mac
findings.detail: Worked-example steps are written as inline $\displaystyle …$ maths, so KaTeX renders them as a .katex span, not a .katex-display (whose overflow-x: auto in css/base.css:153 would make it scroll). The step body .k-n-wm (css/views/study.css:356 .k-n-wbody, no overflow rule) lets the line run on, and on iPhone the step column is only 177px wide (the 'Step' label column takes the rest). The over-wide line widens <main> (scrollWidth 516 vs 402 on S2.1), so the whole topic page can be panned sideways; panned, the step labels leave the screen and the maths bleeds past the card edge. Sweep of all 433 Maths note pages at 402px: 14 lines in 4.1 (4), 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4 (2), 8.3, 8.7, 9.2, S2.1 (2), overflowing by 7-114px. iPad portrait: none.
findings.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/ovf.js → cm/ovf-iphone.json (433 pages, 14 katex lines offscreen), cm/ovf-ipad.json (0); shots/content-maths/top-s21-clip-iphone.png (S2.1 page 4 after the page was panned to the σ line: labels gone, line runs past the card); eval: main.scrollWidth 516 / clientWidth 402 on #/ref/maths/S2.1; js/core/content.js:382 (.k-n-wm wraps para(st.m)); css/views/study.css:351-356
findings.fix: Give .k-n-wm (and other step/answer bodies) overflow-x: auto with the same tab-stop-when-scrolls rule as tables, or render a step whose maths is wider than its column as a display block; on phones stack the Step label above the body to give the maths the full width.
findings.rootCause: Inline \displaystyle maths in a grid cell with no horizontal scroller.

findings.title: On iPhone the Maths plot labs draw their axis numbers at 5.7px (half the 11px label floor)
findings.detail: Every plot lab (lab.plot) writes tick and curve labels at size 14 in the 800-unit viewBox (js/labs/lab.js:252 Math.max(14,…), :317, :321, :325, :382). On iPhone the stage is 326px wide, so the drawing is scaled ×0.41 and every label renders at 5.7 CSS px; the phone crop (lab.js:455-476) does not help a plot because the plot frame fills the viewBox. Measured with getScreenCTM on the Simulations tab: 9.3 Newton–Raphson 16 labels at 5.7px, 9.4 Trapezium rule 21, M7.5 projectiles 18, S4.2 Normal 15, 7.1 21, M9.1 8 at 6.6–7.1px, 10.3 24 at 10.4px. CLAUDE.md invariant 63 sets an 11px label floor for charts. The axis numbers in the screenshot cannot be read without zooming.
findings.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/simtxt.js (iphone/ipad/mac output quoted above); shots/content-maths/top-sim-9-4-iphone.png (dpr 2); shots/content-maths/sim-9-3-iphone.png; js/labs/lab.js:252, :317-326, :481 (lab.narrow)
findings.fix: Scale label size by the stage's px-per-unit (size = 11px / scale, capped) or switch plots to a narrower viewBox when lab.narrow() is true (as the floating-point and subnetting labs do), and thin the ticks (every other tick) so the bigger labels do not collide.
findings.rootCause: Label sizes are fixed in viewBox units, so they shrink with the stage.

findings.title: Cards filed under the wrong leaf
findings.detail: 6.1 (Exponential functions) holds solve-a^x=b items that belong to 6.5: fc3 "Solve $4^x=100$", fc10b "$e^{2x}=5$", fc13b "$2^x=20$", qz3. M8.3 (Weight and gravity) holds suvat projectile items that belong to M7.3: fc13b impact speed and fc14b rebound height. S4.3 (Selecting a distribution) holds normal-approximation and continuity-correction drill that belongs to S4.2: fc10b–fc14b, qz4b, qz5b, qz7b. 2.10 (Partial fractions) qz3 is an integral, ∫2/(x+1), which is 8.6's topic. 10.4 fc8b is an average-speed question. 8.1 fc9b ends without an answer ("a third condition is needed").
findings.evidence: cm/load.js dumps; read with the node print script (outputs quoted in this audit); bank-maths-pure-*.js, bank-maths-mech.js, bank-maths-stats.js | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): No commit to bank-maths-*.js since 56b1a8c; the cards quoted in the first audit are still in place (re-read via cm/load.js).
findings.fix: Move these items to their own leaves, keeping each card's original key as a whole-key third element (invariant 87), or replace them with items on the leaf's own skill.
findings.rootCause: Bank items were grouped by past-paper question rather than by spec point.

findings.title: "Past-paper patterns" pages are one wall-of-text paragraph
findings.detail: 55 of the 57 note paragraphs over 60 words sit on the bank's "Past-paper patterns" page. That is one per leaf, up to 135 words of run-on text with bold phrases and inline series lists. This goes against the user's rule of short lines and bullets, not paragraphs. On M7.3 page 8, one 6-line paragraph lists every question shape, and the lower half of the page is empty. It also repeats the M7.3 overview table of question shapes on page 1.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-pastpaper-mac.png; js/data/content/bank-maths-*.js (each X(…) notes: [{page:"Past-paper patterns"}, "<long string>"]); counted by a script: 57 paragraphs over 60 words, 55 after the bank page | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): Re-counted: 64 paragraphs on 'Past-paper patterns' pages, 59 of them over 60 words, the longest 157 words (count method differs slightly from the first audit's 57).
findings.fix: Convert each to a {table:{head:[Question shape, Marks, Seen in]}} or a {ul} of one shape per line, or fold it into the leaf's existing overview table and drop the page.
findings.rootCause: The bank files were written as prose summaries before the short-lines rule.

findings.title: 29 leaves have no figure where a picture would teach
findings.detail: Leaves with figs=0: 2.1 2.2 2.10 2.11 3.4 4.1 4.2 4.3 4.4 4.5 4.6 5.5 5.6 5.8 5.9 6.4 6.5 7.2 7.4 7.5 7.6 8.1 8.2 8.5 8.6 8.7 8.8 9.5 S3.3. Clear candidates: 5.9 Trig in context (Ferris wheel or tide curve), 5.6 R-form (the R·sin(θ+α) graph with max and min), 8.7 Separable DEs (family of solution curves, which the spec requires students to sketch), 3.4 Parametric modelling (motion path), 7.5 Implicit differentiation (circle with tangent), 4.2 Sequences (increasing, decreasing and periodic plots), 8.2 and 8.1 (antiderivative family), 2.11 modelling curves. Per the user's notes rule, annotated {fig} diagrams are expected wherever a picture helps.
findings.evidence: cm/metrics.json figs column | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): cm/metrics.json: 29 leaves with no figure (2.1, 2.2, 2.10, 2.11, 3.4, 4.1–4.6, 5.5, 5.6, 5.8, 5.9, 6.4, 6.5, 7.2, 7.4–7.6, 8.1, 8.2, 8.5–8.8, 9.5, S3.3). All 184 existing figures render without an error (cm/figs.js).
findings.fix: Add declarative {fig} diagrams (core/figures.js) to these leaves during the depth pass. They are SVG-declarative, so no raster art is needed.
findings.rootCause: Figures were added only as each section was rewritten at depth.

findings.title: Units such as "m s$^{-1}$" break across lines
findings.detail: Units are authored as "m s$^{-1}$" with a normal space. At wrap points the line breaks inside the unit, leaving "…5 m s" at a line end and "−1" on the next line. Seen in M7.2's worked question in Dawn on the Mac ("travels at a constant 5 m s / −1 for the next 15 seconds").
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/m72-notes-dawn-mac.png | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): No change to the content files or css since 56b1a8c (git log empty); not re-shot on this build — shots/content-maths/m72-notes-dawn-mac.png from the first audit.
findings.fix: Author units as a single KaTeX segment, e.g. $\text{m s}^{-1}$ or $5\ \text{m}\,\text{s}^{-1}$, or have inline() replace the space before a unit with U+00A0 and wrap the unit in a white-space:nowrap span.
findings.rootCause: A breakable space plus a separate math segment for the exponent.

findings.title: Two-option quiz items in a 4-option quiz
findings.detail: 8.1 qz9 ("$\int_2^5 f = -\int_5^2 f$ is: true / false") and 4.5 qz12 have only two options, so a guess is right 50% of the time, and they look different from the other items.
findings.evidence: cm/dups.json quizBad entries maths:8.1 #9 and maths:4.5 #12 (bank-maths-pure-c.js, bank-maths-pure-b.js) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): cm/beh1.js re-run: quizBad still maths:4.5 Q13 and maths:8.1 Q10 (bank items with 2 options).
findings.fix: Rewrite them as 4-option items, or as flashcards.
findings.rootCause: Bank authoring.

findings.title: A worked example citing two questions becomes a 4-mark exam item whose scheme covers 7 marks
findings.detail: 7.1 'Prove d/dx(x^3) = 3x^2; and y = 2x^2' has src 'AS June 2018 · P1 Q10 · 4 marks; A-level June 2022 · P2 Q4 · 3 marks'. examFromWorked takes only the FIRST 'N marks' (/(\d+)\s*marks?/.exec). The resulting exam item is marked 4 marks and labelled AS, but its question has parts (i) and (ii) worth 7. Its src string also keeps '· 4 marks; A-level June 2022 · P2 Q4', because only a trailing '· N marks' is stripped.
findings.evidence: eval: KOS_CONTENT['maths:7.1'].exam item → {marks:4, src:'Edexcel June 2018 · P1 Q10 · 4 marks; A-level June 2022 · P2 Q4', level:'AS'}; js/core/content.js:542-546
findings.fix: Either split the worked example into two cards (one per question), or have examFromWorked sum every 'N marks' in src and strip each. The first is cleaner.

findings.title: Normal-distribution generator writes the symmetric interval backwards, e.g. P(61 < X < 51)
findings.detail: When the random x is below μ (89 of 200 runs), the 'Complements you might need' step prints P(2μ − x < X < x). Example: X ~ N(56, 2²), x = 51 gives 'P(61 < X < 51) = 0.9876'. That is an empty interval written as if it were the answer.
findings.evidence: eval on slot 7: normal solve with {mu:56,sg:2,x:51} → 'P(61 < X < 51) = 0.9876 (symmetric interval about μ)'; js/labs/worked.js:549
findings.fix: Print P(min(x, 2μ−x) < X < max(x, 2μ−x)).

findings.title: Hypothesis-test generators draw contradictory set-ups (testing p < p0 with x far above the mean)
findings.detail: The 'hyptest' generator (S5.2) draws the tail and x independently. In 187 of 400 random examples, x lies on the wrong side of the mean for the alternative being tested. Example: H1: p < 0.4 with n = 17 and x = 15 gives P(X ≤ 15) = 1.00000. The example is formally right but teaches nothing, and no exam question is set up that way. The projectile generator also prints '−0 = 20T − 4.9T²' and '4.9T² − 20T − 0 = 0' whenever h = 0 (174 of 400 runs). The partial-fractions and normal-parameters generators print unbracketed double signs: '(5·-1 + -1) / (-1 − 1)' and 'μ = 25 − -0.9945 × 8.0963'.
findings.evidence: eval on slot 7 (400-run sweeps of every one of the 36 Maths generators: no exceptions or NaN; hyptestSilly 187/400; projectile '−0' 174/400); js/labs/worked.js:752 (hyptest random); js/labs/worked-extra.js:356-373 (projectile)
findings.fix: hyptest: draw x from the alternative's side (below n·p0 for 'lower'), and draw h in the projectile generator only when h > 0 or drop the term. Use a shared signed formatter that brackets negatives inside a product or after a minus sign.

findings.title: Seven Maths callouts use an undefined kind 'key' and render as an unlabelled teal Tip
findings.detail: The callout schema (js/core/content.js:31, CALLOUT_META :49-58) knows info, def, tip, warn, miscon, mnemonic, memorise and formula. Seven Maths callouts in 1.1, 9.2, 9.3 and 10.x use t:'key'. The renderer falls back to the Tip icon (◆), and the stylesheet has no [data-kind=key] rule, so they get the base teal, the same as info and formula. The author meant a 'key idea' box, but on the page it cannot be told apart from an ordinary formula or info box.
findings.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/beh1.js output 'bad callout types: key 7'; grep -rn 't: "key"' js/data/content → maths-pure-p1.js:152, maths-pure-p10.js:27, :437 and maths-pure-p9.js; js/core/content.js:346 (CALLOUT_META[t] || tip); css/views/study.css:321-334 (no key rule)
findings.fix: Either add a 'key' kind to CALLOUT_META and the stylesheet (e.g. 'Key idea', crimson), or change the seven to an existing kind. Then make validate_content.js reject unknown callout kinds.

findings.title: Two bank items depend on the item before them and break when the quiz is shuffled (M8.4 'Tension then:')
findings.detail: The M8.4 bank item Q6 reads only 'Tension then:' (options 0 / 39.2 N / 78.4 N / 19.6 N). It relies on Q5 ('Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley'). The quiz has a Shuffle control that reorders the questions (js/engines/quiz.js:66), so after a shuffle, or when Q6 appears alone in a review of missed items, the question has no data. A sweep of all 1,058 Maths quiz stems found no other stem that leans on the previous item: the 'then' in 4.1, M7.1 and M9.1 completes the sentence.
findings.evidence: js/data/content/bank-maths-mech.js (M8.4 quiz, items 5–6); node print of maths:M8.4 quiz: 'Q5b Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley. Acceleration: … Q6b Tension then:'; stem-dependency regex sweep over KOS_CONTENT maths quiz
findings.fix: Make Q6 self-contained: 'Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley. The tension is:'.

findings.title: 6.4 flashcard question mixes base 2 and base 10 in one garbled stem
findings.detail: The 6.4 bank card reads 'Solve log_2(x+3) + log_2(x+10) = 2 + 2log_2 x… with base 10 and 2 = log 100.' The answer works in base 10 ((x+3)(x+10) = 100x², x = 0.620), so the stem is a half-edited sentence. Read as written (base 2), the answer would be (x+3)(x+10) = 4x², giving x = 6, which is a different answer.
findings.evidence: js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-b.js:739
findings.fix: Rewrite the stem as 'Solve log(x+3) + log(x+10) = 2 + 2 log x (base 10).'

findings.title: A third of Maths quiz explanations are a bare label: 352 of 1,058 'why' lines are three words or fewer with no working ('Definition.' ×9, 'Chain rule.' ×9, 'Add.', 'Tables.')
findings.detail: After a wrong answer the quiz shows the item's 'why' as the explanation. In 352 of 1,058 Maths quiz items (99 base, 253 bank) it is three words or fewer with no maths: 'Definition.' ×9, 'Chain rule.' ×9, 'Power law.' ×5, 'Product rule.', 'Multiply.', 'Add.', 'Tables.', 'Vertex.', 'Union.', 'Conjugate.'. A learner who picked the wrong option is told the name of a rule, not why their option was wrong or what the right working is. The bank files are the main source (253 of 560 bank items vs 99 of 498 base).
findings.evidence: node one-liner over cm/load.js (KOS_CONTENT maths quiz): 352/1058 label-only, by source {base 99, bank 253}; examples: maths:2.2 Q11 'Conjugate.', maths:2.3 Q14 'Vertex.', maths:2.5 Q10 'Union.'; js/data/content/bank-maths-*.js
findings.fix: Rewrite the label-only whys as one line of working that names the misconception behind the most tempting wrong option (e.g. 'Multiply by the conjugate $3-\sqrt7$, so the denominator becomes $9-7=2$').
findings.rootCause: Bank items were authored with terse whys and no length/quality check in validate_content.

findings.title: Four Pure leaf titles show raw caret notation ('e^x', 'Gradient of e^kx', 'Solving a^x = b', 'Differentiating x^n, e^kx…') in the spine, heading and search
findings.detail: The SHORT title table in tools/gen_data.py writes four titles in ASCII maths: 6.1 'Exponential functions & e^x', 6.2 'Gradient of e^kx', 6.5 'Solving a^x = b', 7.2 'Differentiating x^n, e^kx, trig, ln x'. Titles are plain text (the spine, the page h1, breadcrumbs, search results, Reports and the Assistant all print them as-is), so the learner sees literal carets in an otherwise typeset subject.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/top-51-fig-azure-ipadl.png (spine: 'Exponential functions & e^x', 'Gradient of e^kx', 'Solving a^x = b'); tools/gen_data.py SHORT entries 6.1, 6.2, 6.5, 7.2; js/data/maths.js:521
findings.fix: Use Unicode superscripts in the titles (eˣ, eᵏˣ, aˣ, xⁿ) in the SHORT table and regenerate js/data/maths.js with --format-existing.
findings.rootCause: Generated titles are plain strings written with ASCII exponents.

qol: Shuffle the options (not just the questions) in the MCQ engine, keeping the authored answer mapped
Show the mark total beside each worked example's codes so authors and learners see a mismatch
A 'Retry missed' banner that says it is practice and does not change the score
Phone layout for worked steps: label above the working so maths gets the full width
backlog: Deepen the thin core leaves (8.4, 8.1, 6.1, 6.2, 4.3, 7.2, 8.6) to the 4.1/M7.x depth with figures
Regenerate the Maths spec text from a clean source (spec PDF re-extraction with fraction/superscript handling) and short S/M titles
A content lint in validate_content for Maths: duplicate cards across base/bank, worked mark sums, label-only whys, callout kinds, two-option items, stem dependencies
Fork staleness: store the shipped hash in a fork and offer 'the shipped notes changed — compare/reset'
